summary: Lee County, VA peak on Stone Mountain where a December 1940 work crew attempted a fire tower for the Virginia Department of Forestry; listed as gone, and no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source checked gives a removal date or describes what remains.

events.note: December 1940 item says a CCC crew had attempted to build a fire tower on the peak of Pine Knob; the item does not say the tower was finished

evidence.supports: Pine Knob in Lee County, placed on Stone Mountain
evidence.quote: peak of Pine Knob, Stone Mountain

evidence.supports: Virginia Department of Forestry is the listed agency
work crew had attempted the task of building a fire tower on the peak
evidence.quote: have attempted the task of constructing a fire tower on the peak of Pine Knob, Stone Mountain.

evidence.supports: crew carried heavy timber up the mountain for 1.6 miles
evidence.quote: carry the heavy timber for this tower up the mountain for 1.6 miles

evidence.supports: material carried up without an accident
evidence.quote: carrying the material up the mountain without an accident.

evidence.supports: item is from a CCC company
evidence.quote: Smoker Over - CCC, Company 2380, Jonesville, Va.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia describes an old tower site on Stone Mountain with views over the Powell River
evidence.quote: There are good views across the Powell river to Powell Mountain from an old tower site on Stone Mountain.

notes_for_editor: Only one 1940 item describes the tower, and it says construction was being attempted, not that it was finished. The Wikipedia 'old tower site' may or may not be Pine Knob; the article does not name it, so it is not cited for identity. No NHLR or FFLOS record for Pine Knob was in the crawl cache, and the firetower.org guessed URL returned 404. Access is left out because no source covers it.
